problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Two Euclidean planar domains and their scalar Laplacians
problem_fingerprint.domain: Bounded strictly convex open subsets of R^2
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: C-infinity boundaries; full infinite spectra including multiplicities
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: Every such pair of domains; no closeness or symmetry hypothesis
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Equality of every indexed eigenvalue implies congruence
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Standard Euclidean Laplacian with no variable density or potential; exact spectra without rescaling
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Omega_2=Q Omega_1+a for Q in O(2) and a in R^2
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Exact identifiability; neither numerical reconstruction nor stability is asserted

statement_source_and_scope_match: Smooth strictly convex subcase of LMP Open Problem 6.2.26(ii); DSKW §1 independently states the inverse spectral problem for smooth convex classes. Strict convexity means each open chord between distinct closure points lies in the domain; no positive curvature convention is silently imposed.
proposed_statement_text: If two bounded strictly convex open subsets of R^2 have C-infinity boundaries and identical Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalue multisets, must a Euclidean isometry map one onto the other?
applied_significance: In the ideal homogeneous membrane model with known tension and density and fixed boundary, the square roots of Dirichlet eigenvalues give vibration frequencies up to a known factor. The question asks whether complete exact frequency data identify a convex membrane shape.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.difference: Boundary-distance recovery uses labeled geometric measurements rather than the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiset.
Billiard integrability characterizes ellipses; does not assert global inverse spectral uniqueness.
Eigenvalue inequalities concern extremal bounds rather than full-spectrum identifiability.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: No equivalent full Dirichlet spectral determination assertion among baseline or five accepted drafts.
implications_or_equivalences: Do not count smooth nonconvex, Neumann, deformation-rigidity or convex parameter restrictions as automatic additional entries.
DSKW and Koval relate billiards and spectra but their theorems do not equate general integrability with spectral determination.

open_status_evidence_summary: LMP explicitly lists convex and smooth planar isospectrality as open; independent DSKW §1 explains the unresolved smooth convex inverse problem. Current searches locate restricted Dirichlet uniqueness and Steklov counterexamples, not full Dirichlet resolution.
independent_status_corroboration: DSKW authors are disjoint from LMP authors; their introduction explicitly distinguishes the unresolved inverse problem from deformation rigidity.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: Disks and sufficiently low-eccentricity ellipses are determined globally; Koval proves local spectral uniqueness for ellipses outside a small exceptional set. These do not cover arbitrary pairs of smooth strictly convex domains.

issues_found: Current near-circle Laplace rigidity is stronger than the generic 2017 corollary; read HZ full main theorems.
Ordinary Steklov equality must not be confused with strong Steklov isospectrality, which includes extra spectral data.
